title: Predicting transcriptional outcomes of novel multigene perturbations with GEARS
authors: Roohani Y, Huang K, Leskovec J
what_it_does: Deep-learning model that predicts transcriptional responses to single and multigene perturbations from Perturb-seq data; full text confirms it uses a gene co-expression graph for gene embeddings and a Gene Ontology-derived graph for perturbation embeddings.
differentiation: GEARS predicts transcriptomic perturbation outcomes using GO and co-expression graphs (full text has no CORUM, STRING or protein-complex prior). We use curated complex membership to impute and select single-cell proteins.

title: A comprehensive benchmark of sequence-based subcellular localization predictors for human proteins
authors: Wefers Z, Gupta A, Ahmed N, Zhang X, Lundberg E
what_it_does: Benchmark (3,814 human proteins) of sequence-based subcellular-localization predictors and PLM/aggregation combinations. The full text adds a ProtT5-MHA-PPI variant with GraphSAGE layers trained on BioPlex 3.0 or STRING; it 'did not substansially [sic] outperform ProtT5-MHA by any average metric', and PPI edges helped only proteins whose interactors mostly share a compartment.
differentiation: Task is protein localization from sequence, not single-cell proteomic state, and it used generic PPI (STRING/BioPlex), not curated complexes. It is a cautionary negative result for generic-PPI GNN priors, which supports our STRING-vs-complex comparison, but it is not a direct collision.

title: AROMA: Augmented Reasoning Over a Multimodal Architecture for Virtual Cell Genetic Perturbation Modeling
authors: Wang Z, Ye G, Liu W, Ng MTA
what_it_does: LLM-based (Qwen3-8B core per paper) virtual-cell model that predicts perturbation-target gene effects with interpretable reasoning, using text, graph topology and protein-sequence features. Its Gene-KG merges STRING edges with CORUM complexes expanded to pairwise edges, collapsing all evidence types into one undirected graph.
differentiation: Strong overlap on knowledge sources (STRING + CORUM), but AROMA merges them indistinguishably for transcriptional perturbation prediction. We isolate complex membership as the prior, test it against STRING and a degree-preserving shuffle, and apply it to single-cell proteomics imputation and panel selection.

title: MAP: A Knowledge-driven Framework for Predicting Single-cell Responses for Unprofiled Drugs
authors: Feng J, Zhao Z, Zhang X, ... Xie W
what_it_does: Builds MAP-KG, a knowledge graph unifying 14 public resources (187k drugs, 23k genes, 694k relationships), and uses knowledge-aligned gene/drug embeddings with a single-cell foundation model for zero-shot chemical-perturbation response prediction.
differentiation: A separate project from AROMA, not part of it. It covers drug-response prediction from transcriptomics. Whether CORUM is among its 14 resources is UNVERIFIED (the abstract does not list them).
unverified_note: Component list of MAP-KG not checked (bioRxiv full text rate-limited); CORUM inclusion unverified.

title: Fuzzy-FishNET: a highly reproducible protein complex-based approach for feature selection in comparative proteomics
authors: Goh WWB
what_it_does: Replaces the t-test in hypergeometric complex-enrichment with a fuzzy rank-based weighting, then selects class-discriminative protein complexes with high feature-selection reproducibility on simulated and real proteomics data.
differentiation: Strong conceptual overlap: protein complexes as the unit of proteomics feature selection. It works on bulk comparative proteomics for class discrimination and does no imputation, single-cell analysis or random-walk panel design.

title: Associating genes and protein complexes with disease via network propagation
authors: Vanunu O, Magger O, Ruppin E, Shlomi T, Sharan R
what_it_does: Global network-propagation method (smoothness over a PPI network plus prior information) for prioritizing disease genes. It also infers disease-associated protein complexes (139 coherent complexes across 1,369 OMIM diseases).
differentiation: We reuse the propagation idea (RWR) for proteomic panel selection on a complex-membership graph. PRINCE already scores complexes, but for disease-gene prioritization, not measurement design or imputation.

title: Classification with Missing Data - A NIFty Pipeline for Single-Cell Proteomics
authors: Nitz AA, Echarry B, McGee B, Payne SH
what_it_does: Top-scoring-pairs feature selection plus classification pipeline for SCP that needs no pre-imputed data, avoids double dipping and tolerates batch effects. Code: https://github.com/PayneLab/nifty (repo described as 'Never Impute Features'); manuscript code: https://github.com/PayneLab/nifty-manuscript. It uses Petrosius et al. data from MassIVE MSV000095333 (Exp6) among its datasets.
differentiation: Same problem (missingness-tolerant SCP feature selection) with no biological prior. It is a natural baseline: we add curated-complex priors. Note that it already benchmarks on a Petrosius dataset.

title: PCIPG2.0: multi-omics fusion and structure-aware graph autoencoding for protein complex identification
authors: Huang Y, Wang J, Yang L, Gong X
what_it_does: Unsupervised framework that completes the PPI interactome using multi-omics views and learns residue-informed protein embeddings with a PPI graph autoencoder to infer complex memberships; benchmarked on five yeast benchmarks. Code: https://github.com/hyx-1/PCIPG2.0.
differentiation: PCIPG2.0 predicts complexes. We consume curated complexes as a prior for single-cell protein-state reconstruction. Its predicted complexes could at most be an alternative prior.

title: scPROTEIN: a versatile deep graph contrastive learning framework for single-cell proteomics embedding
authors: Li W, Yang F, Wang F, Rong Y, Liu L, Wu B, Zhang H, Yao J
what_it_does: Peptide-uncertainty estimation (multitask heteroscedastic regression) plus graph-contrastive cell embedding for SCP: denoising, batch correction, clustering and annotation.
differentiation: Learns cell embeddings from the data without a curated protein-complex prior. The abstract does not specify the graph construction; 'cell–cell graph' is our paraphrase, not verified from the abstract.

title: scProfiterole: Clustering of Single-Cell Proteomic Data Using Graph Contrastive Learning via Spectral Filters
authors: Coşkun M, Lopes FB, Kubilay Tolunay P, Chance MR, Koyutürk M
venue: Journal of Computational Biology (online 2026-10-09); preprint bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.02.26.708196
what_it_does: Graph contrastive learning on cell-to-cell similarity graphs from SCP profiles, using Arnoldi-based polynomial interpolation of spectral filters (heat/beta kernels) for clustering.
differentiation: Uses cell-cell graphs for clustering. We use protein-protein (complex) graphs for imputation and panel selection.

title: STRING MCP Server (official)
authors: STRING consortium / meringlab (von Mering lab GitHub org)
venue: Web service: https://mcp.string-db.org/ ; code https://github.com/meringlab/string-mcp (MIT, per help page)
what_it_does: Official remote MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP) exposing STRING identifier resolution, interaction networks/figures, functional enrichment, annotation, homology search and evidence links. Self-hostable from meringlab/string-mcp.
differentiation: Covers generic PPI (STRING) only. Our MCP server exposes curated-complex imputation and panel-selection tools and could run alongside or call STRING-MCP for the STRING baseline.

title: MCPmed: A Call for MCP-Enabled Bioinformatics Web Services for LLM-Driven Discovery
authors: Flotho M, Diks IF, Flotho P, Molano LAG, Hirsch P, Keller A
venue: arXiv:2507.08055; journal version Briefings in Bioinformatics 27(1):bbag076 (2026)
what_it_does: Proposes MCP layers for bioinformatics web-server backends, with implementations for GEO, STRING and UCSC Cell Browser, plus 'breadcrumbs' and templates; code at https://github.com/MCPmed.
differentiation: A community effort we could contribute a CORUM/Complex Portal-backed SCP tool server to. MCPmed itself does no imputation or complex-prior modelling.

title: CORUM: the comprehensive resource of mammalian protein complexes-2022
authors: Tsitsiridis G, Steinkamp R, Giurgiu M, Brauner B, Fobo G, Frishman G, Montrone C, Ruepp A
what_it_does: CORUM 4.0: 5,204 manually curated mammalian complexes from 5,299 genes (26% of human protein-coding genes).
differentiation: Data source for our complex prior; cite the CORUM 5.0 paper if using the current release.

title: CORUM in 2024: protein complexes as drug targets
authors: Steinkamp R, Tsitsiridis G, Brauner B, Montrone C, Fobo G, Frishman G, Avram S, Oprea TI, Ruepp A
what_it_does: CORUM 5.0: 7,193 manually curated mammalian complexes, plus 1,975 literature instances of drugs affecting complex formation or function (DrugCentral targets).
differentiation: Primary citation for the current CORUM release used as our prior.

title: Complex portal 2025: predicted human complexes and enhanced visualisation tools for the comparison of orthologous and paralogous complexes
authors: Balu S, Huget S, Medina Reyes JJ, Ragueneau E, Panneerselvam K, ... Rappsilber J, ... (16 authors)
what_it_does: Manually curated complex database (28 species): 2,150 curated human complexes augmented with 14,964 ML-predicted complexes from hu.MAP3.0, plus the Complex Navigator visualisation.
differentiation: Data source. If we use only curated complexes we must filter out the hu.MAP3.0-predicted ones; mixing them changes what the prior means.

title: Widespread Post-transcriptional Attenuation of Genomic Copy-Number Variation in Cancer
authors: Gonçalves E, Fragoulis A, Garcia-Alonso L, Cramer T, Saez-Rodriguez J, Beltrao P
what_it_does: In CPTAC/TCGA tumours, CNVs are post-transcriptionally buffered in 23-33% of proteins, which are enriched in complex members; complex subunits are highly co-regulated, and some are rate-limiting for assembly (48 interactions; AP3B1-AP3M1 and GTF2E2-GTF2E1 confirmed).
differentiation: Bulk-tumour evidence for why complex partners should predict a missing protein's abundance; we test this as a prior in single cells.

title: Multi-omics Characterization of Interaction-mediated Control of Human Protein Abundance levels
authors: Sousa A, Gonçalves E, Mirauta B, Ochoa D, Stegle O, Beltrao P
what_it_does: Up to 42% of 8,124 proteins show post-transcriptional control; it finds interaction-dependent abundance control for 516 protein pairs (correlated with interface size), likely via degradation of unassembled complex subunits.
differentiation: Mechanistic support for partner-weighted imputation, from bulk data.

title: Exploring functional protein covariation across single cells using nPOP
authors: Leduc A, Huffman RG, Cantlon J, Khan S, Slavov N
what_it_does: nPOP droplet sample prep for thousands of single cells; protein covariation analysis reveals cell-cycle dynamics and metabolic (OXPHOS vs glycolysis, ribosomal) covariation in melanoma subpopulations.
differentiation: Contrary to the starting hypothesis, it does not analyse protein-complex covariation: 'complex' appears once in the full text, in an introductory sentence that covariation 'may reflect protein interactions within complexes'. It is weaker support than the hypothesis assumed and not a direct overlap.

title: Evaluating the capabilities of the Astral mass analyzer for single-cell proteomics
authors: Petrosius V, Aragon-Fernandez P, Arrey TN, Üresin N, Furtwängler B, Stewart H, Denisov E, Petzoldt J, Peterson AC, Hock C, Damoc E, Makarov A, Zabrouskov V, Porse BT, Schoof EM
venue: bioRxiv (posted 2023-06-08; bioRxiv API reports no linked published version)
what_it_does: Evaluates the Orbitrap Astral with DIA for ultra-low input and single cells; shows cell-cycle dynamics in HEK293 and heterogeneity in the primary AML culture model OCI-AML8227 (full text). It plots MCM helicase subunit trends but does no CORUM-based analysis.
differentiation: Our benchmark dataset. Dataverse doi:10.14428/DVN/4DSPJM ('Astral AML single-cell data from Petrosius et al. 2023 preprint', deposited by L. Gatto) cites this preprint as its publication.

title: Quantitative Label-Free Single-Cell Proteomics on the Orbitrap Astral MS
authors: Petrosius V, Aragon-Fernandez P, Arrey TN, Woessmann J, Üresin N, de Boer B, Su J, Furtwängler B, ... (18 authors)
what_it_does: Published Astral SCP methods paper (from preprint 10.1101/2024.07.31.605978). It profiles HEK293, U937 and primary BM CD34+ cells and, 'as a proof of concept', shows that covariation of known complexes (MCM complex, proteasome subunits) is captured in scp-MS data.
differentiation: Direct overlap on mechanism: the same group shows complex covariation in Astral SCP. They use it descriptively, not as an imputation or panel-selection prior, and it does not include the OCI-AML8227 cells (no 'OCI-AML'/'8227' in the full text), so it is not the citation for our dataset.

title: The STRING database in 2023: protein-protein association networks and functional enrichment analyses for any sequenced genome of interest
authors: Szklarczyk D, Kirsch R, Koutrouli M, Nastou K, Mehryary F, Hachilif R, Gable AL, Fang T, Doncheva NT, Pyysalo S, Bork P, Jensen LJ, von Mering C
what_it_does: Describes STRING v12.0, which integrates physical and functional associations from text mining, co-expression, genomic context, experiments and 'known complexes/pathways from curated sources'.
differentiation: Generic-PPI baseline. STRING already includes curated complex knowledge, so the complex-vs-STRING comparison must control for the overlap (e.g. STRING minus complex edges).

title: The STRING database in 2025: protein networks with directionality of regulation
authors: Szklarczyk D, Nastou K, Koutrouli M, Kirsch R, Mehryary F, Hachilif R, Hu D, Peluso ME, Huang Q, Fang T, Doncheva NT, Pyysalo S, Bork P, Jensen LJ, von Mering C
what_it_does: Describes STRING 12.5: a new regulatory network (type and directionality), with separate functional, physical and regulatory networks and improved enrichment.
differentiation: Cite if using STRING 12.5 (e.g. its separate physical network as a stricter PPI baseline).

title: Genenames.org: the HGNC and PGNC resources in 2026
authors: Seal RL, Braschi B, Gray K, McClay J, Tweedie S, Bruford EA
what_it_does: HGNC update: >44,400 approved symbols (>19,250 protein-coding); introduces the Plant Gene Nomenclature Committee.
differentiation: Used for gene-symbol harmonisation across CORUM, Complex Portal, STRING and the SCP data.

title: Recovering biological structure in sparse single-cell proteomics with GIRAFI
authors: Zhong H, Chi S, Wong R, Rogalski J, Wang Z, Chan S, Bailey ML, Ebrahimi A, ... Foster LJ, Tang X (16 authors)
what_it_does: Graph-informed statistical imputation for SCP that constrains inference to dataset-aware, prior-knowledge-informed protein neighbourhoods. Per the full text, the prior is 'a curated PPI prior downloaded from STRINGdb version 11.5', fused with data-derived correlations via λ; the authors say it 'primarily relies on data-derived protein associations while using curated PPI information as a modest prior'. Code to be released at https://github.com/dorothyzh/GIRAFI.
differentiation: The closest collision: graph-prior imputation for SCP already exists. It uses a STRING prior, CORUM appears only in its reference list, and the fetched text shows no degree-preserving-shuffle control and no OCI-AML8227/Astral data. Our claim must be framed as 'which prior' (curated complexes vs STRING vs shuffled), with GIRAFI as a baseline.

title: Protrec2: tissue-specific network-based missing protein recovery method
authors: Kong W, Goh WWB, Wong L
what_it_does: Probabilistic framework that combines tissue-specific protein-complex annotations with Bayesian inference to recover unreported but present proteins in (bulk) proteomes; benchmarked on HeLa/A549 and lung tumour-normal pairs against CPTAC.
differentiation: Uses complex membership to recover missing proteins, which overlaps our prior. It works on bulk proteomes and predicts presence (detection), not single-cell quantitative imputation or panel selection.

title: The complexome contextualizes proteomics data to fingerprint biological states and highlight perturbed functional modules in disease
authors: Guharoy M, Adant I, Bird M, Botzki A, Collier J, ... (23 authors)
what_it_does: Framework using curated complexes (the 'complexome') as the unit for integrating proteomics data, fingerprinting tissues and detecting perturbed complexes (e.g. OXPHOS) in patient fibroblasts; code https://github.com/mguharoy/Complexome.
differentiation: Same 'complexes as the interpretive unit' idea, but descriptive and on bulk data. It does no imputation, single-cell analysis, panel selection or comparison against STRING/shuffled priors.

title: ToolUniverse: An open platform for democratizing AI scientists
authors: Gao S, Zhu R, Sui P, Kong Z, Aldogom S, Huang Y, Noori A, Shamji R, Parvataneni K, Tsiligkaridis T, Zitnik M
what_it_does: Platform standardising >2,700 scientific tools for AI agents, accessible via Python, HTTP and MCP (connector https://aiscientist.tools/mcp). Its source includes a Complex Portal tool with search_complexes (complexes containing a gene/protein) and get_complex operations.
differentiation: Already provides agent access to complex lookup (gene → Complex Portal complexes), so a bare 'complex lookup MCP' is not novel. Our tools add complex-prior imputation and RWR panel selection on SCP data. No CORUM tool was found in the fetched pages.

title: BioContextAI is a community hub for agentic biomedical systems
authors: Kuehl M, Schaub DP, Carli F, Heumos L, Hellmig M, Fernández-Zapata C, Kaiser N, Schaul J, Kulaga A, Usanov N, ... (20 authors)
what_it_does: Open-source initiative centred on MCP servers: a community registry of biomedical MCP servers plus a proof-of-concept knowledgebase server integrating widely used biomedical knowledgebases.
differentiation: A registry where our server could be listed. The exact knowledgebases in its server (a web-search summary mentioned STRING, OmniPath, Reactome) were not verified from a primary page.

title: hu.MAP3.0: atlas of human protein complexes by integration of >25,000 proteomic experiments
authors: Fischer SN, Claussen ER, Kourtis S, Sdelci S, Orchard S, Hermjakob H, Kustatscher G, Drew K
what_it_does: >15,000 ML-derived human complexes from >25,000 MS experiments, characterised with ProteomeHD.2 covariation; imported into Complex Portal.
differentiation: Candidate alternative or larger complex prior. It is predicted, not manually curated, so it should be a separate arm, not mixed with CORUM.

title: A tissue-specific atlas of protein-protein associations enables prioritization of candidate disease genes
authors: Laman Trip DS, van Oostrum M, Memon D, Frommelt F, Baptista D, Panneerselvam K, Bradley G, Licata L, Hermjakob H, Orchard S, Trynka G, McDonagh EM, ...
what_it_does: Protein co-abundance across 7,811 proteomic samples from 11 tissues recapitulates known complexes; stable-complex interactions are well preserved across tissues, and >25% of associations are tissue-specific.
differentiation: Bulk evidence that complex co-abundance is robust across contexts, which supports a curated-complex prior over a generic network.

title: Complex assembly and activity states as multifaceted protein attributes explaining phenotypic variability
authors: Rosenberger G, Xue P, Bludau I, Martelli C, Williams E, Collins BC, Califano A, Liu Y, Aebersold R
what_it_does: Multi-omics framework inferring protein activities via network diffusion. Protein correlation profiling gives 'direct evidence that complex assembly buffers variation in gene copy number and transcription' in HeLa lines.
differentiation: Supports complex-assembly buffering, and uses network diffusion (related to our RWR), but in bulk HeLa variants, not SCP imputation.

title: Relating transcriptomics to protein abundance reveals self-driven versus interactor-driven proteins
authors: Arnaout L, Helms V, Papazian A
what_it_does: Regresses CPTAC protein abundance on a gene's own transcript and the transcripts of its STRING interaction partners. It finds 'interaction-driven' genes (e.g. ribosome) whose protein levels are explained mainly by partners' transcripts.
differentiation: Partner-based prediction of protein abundance from bulk mRNA with STRING partners. We predict from measured partner proteins in single cells with complex membership.

title: Protein-protein interactions shape trans-regulatory impact of genetic variation on protein expression and complex traits
authors: Li J, Li YI, Liu X
what_it_does: trans-pQTLs are enriched at PPI interfaces; PPI-guided trans-pQTL mapping finds 17,662 trans-pQTLs affecting 961 PPI clusters, linking GWAS loci to protein complexes.
differentiation: Closest find for 'variant → complex' reasoning, but it is a statistical-genetics analysis, not a lookup tool. No dedicated variant-to-complex lookup tool was found.

title: Proteomics Data Imputation With a Deep Model That Learns From Many Datasets
authors: Harris L, Noble WS
what_it_does: Lupine: deep imputation model trained jointly on many datasets (CPTAC TMT, >1,000 samples), outperforming prior proteomics imputation methods.
differentiation: Data-driven bulk imputation with no biological prior; a possible 'data alone' baseline.

title: Learning from natural variation across the proteomes of single cells
authors: Slavov N
what_it_does: Perspective: biological functions arise from protein interactions reflected in natural proteome variation across single cells, which SCP may decode.
differentiation: Conceptual framing for our hypothesis; it makes no method or benchmark claim.
